arxiv-2112-12406.title: Revisiting Shikhmurzaev’s approach to the contact line problem
arxiv-2112-12406.creator: Amrita Ghosh, Barbara Niethammer, Juan J.L. Velázquez
arxiv-2112-12406.description: Abstract In this paper, we revisit a model for the contact line problem which has been proposed by Shikhmurzaev (1993). In the first part, in addition to rederiving the model, we study in detail the assumptions required to obtain the isothermal limit of the model. We also derive in this paper several lubrication approximation models, based on Shikhmurzaev’s approach.

arxiv-2401-17138.title: Nuclear scattering via quantum computing
arxiv-2401-17138.creator: Peiyan Wang, Weijie Du, Wei Zuo, James P. Vary
arxiv-2401-17138.description: Abstract We propose a hybrid quantum-classical framework to solve the elastic scattering phase shift of two well-bound nuclei in an uncoupled channel. Within this framework, we develop a many-body formalism in which the continuum scattering states of the two colliding nuclei are regulated by a weak external harmonic oscillator potential with varying strength.

arxiv-2412-01924.title: Kondo overscreening in the presence of superconductivity.
arxiv-2412-01924.creator: Pradip Kattel, Abay Zhakenov, Natan Andrei
arxiv-2412-01924.description: Abstract We study the interplay and competition between Kondo overscreening and superconductivity. The model we consider consists of a single spin − 1 2 -\frac{1}{2} quantum impurity at the edge of a quantum wire coupled to spin − 1 -1 bulk fermions that interact attractively, generating a (superconducting) mass gap. The competition leads to a rich phase structure.

arxiv-2508-00350.title: BOOD: Boundary-based Out-Of-Distribution Data Generation
arxiv-2508-00350.creator: Qilin Liao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao, Ping Luo, Hengshuang Zhao
arxiv-2508-00350.description: Abstract Harnessing the power of diffusion models to synthesize auxiliary training data based on latent space features has proven effective in enhancing out-of-distribution (OOD) detection performance. However, extracting effective features outside the in-distribution (ID) boundary in latent space remains challenging due to the difficulty of identifying decision boundaries between classes.

arxiv-2509-24630.title: T-duality and bosonization as examples of continuum gauging and disentangling
arxiv-2509-24630.creator: Gertian Roose, Erez Zohar
arxiv-2509-24630.description: Abstract Dualities and duality transformations form a well established methodology in various aspects of quantum many body physics and quantum field theories, allowing one to exploit equivalence between models which may naively seem completely different in order to gain access to further physical regimes, either analytically, numerically or experimentally.

arxiv-2602-17445.title: ABCD: All Biases Come Disguised
arxiv-2602-17445.creator: Mateusz NowakXavier CadetPeter ChinDartmouth College
arxiv-2602-17445.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Mateusz NowakXavier CadetPeter ChinDartmouth College. Multiple-choice question (MCQ) benchmarks have been a standard evaluation practice for measuring LLMs’ ability to reason and answer knowledge-based questions. Through a synthetic NonsenseQA benchmark, we observe that different LLMs exhibit varying degrees of label-position-few-shot-prompt bias, where the model either uses the answer position, the label in front of the answer, the distributions of correct answers present in the few-shot prompt, or a combination of all to answer each MCQ question.

pmc-10775048.title: Conditional survival analysis of patients with resected non–small cell lung cancer
pmc-10775048.creator: Talib Chaudhry, Vaishnavi Krishnan, Andrew E. Donaldson, Zachary M. Palmisano, Sanjib Basu, Nicole M. Geissen, Justin M. Karush, Gillian C. Alex, Jeffrey A. Borgia, Michael J. Liptay, Christopher W. Seder
pmc-10775048.description: BackgroundConditional survival (CS) analyses provide an estimate of survival accounting for years already survived after treatment. We aim to evaluate the difference between actuarial and conditional survival in patients following lung resection for non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In addition, CS analyses are used to examine whether prognosticators of survival change over time following surgery.

pmc-13408402.creator: Mauz ul Haq, Zaryab Khan, Aman Nawaz, Abd Al Karim Jaafar
pmc-13408402.description: Nitrate (NO₃-) leaching from alkaline coarse-textured agricultural soils is a major concern that reduces nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and limits crop productivity. Application of biochar has been found to improve soil fertility through nutrient retention when used with nitrogen fertilizer, however, its efficacy in coarse-textured alkaline soil is insufficiently explored.

pmc-13437611.title: A Refined Injection Strategy for the Upper Third Using Incobotulinum Toxin A to Enhance Facial Harmony and Preserve Natural Expression
pmc-13437611.creator: Massimo Renzi
pmc-13437611.description: The eyebrow is a central anatomical unit in upper facial aesthetics, where multiple muscle groups—including the frontalis, corrugator supercilii, and orbicularis oculi—interact to influence its position and movement. Achieving an optimal balance among these muscles is crucial to enhance facial harmony while preserving natural expressiveness.

pmc-13574280.title: BCX9250 is a potent small-molecule inhibitor of Activin A Receptor Type 1 (ACVR1/ALK2) for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva
pmc-13574280.creator: Haitao Wang, Saman Toutounchi, Robert J Pignolo, Xiaogang Cheng, Cynthia Davis Parker, Qingde Liu, Saritha Muppa, Debra Kellogg-Yelder, Kevin J Polach, Pravin L Kotian, Yarlagadda S Babu, Xilin Chen
pmc-13574280.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is an ultra-rare genetic disease of heterotopic ossification (HO) caused by mutations in the activin receptor-like kinase-2 (ALK2) protein, a BMP type I receptor of the TGF-β superfamily. These mutations in the ALK2 receptor alter receptor function, causing activin A, a protein that normally inhibits ALK2 signaling, to aberrantly trigger suppressor of mothers against decapentaplegic 1/5/8 (SMAD1/5/8) signaling, thereby activating the chondroosteogenic pathway and leading to HO.

uslaw-usc-t16-s460y.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 1 (National Parks, Military Parks, Monuments, And Seashores); Subchapter LXXXIII (King Range National Conservation Area). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary of the Interior (hereinafter referred to as the “Secretary”) is hereby authorized and directed, after compliance with sections 460y–2 and 460y–3 of this title, to establish, within the boundaries described in section 460y–8.
